counterexample.claim_refuted: Arbitrary bounded predictable covariates with IID subjects, positive risk support and nonsingular Cox information imply sup_t risk-sum convergence.
counterexample.construction: Fix tau>0, p=1, beta0=0 and B=[-1,1]. Take mutually independent IID subject records comprising T_i~Exponential(1), C_i=tau, and independent Bernoulli(1/2) variables W_i,B_i1,B_i2,..., all bits known in F0. Let t_k=tau/(k+1), Z_i(t)=B_ik at t=t_k and Z_i(t)=W_i otherwise. Use the common filtration generated by all bits and each event history through t. Set Y_i(t)=1{min(T_i,tau)>=t}, N_i(t)=1{T_i<=t}, and A_i(t)=integral_0^t Y_i(u)du.
counterexample.model_verification: The covariate is jointly measurable and predictable: its countably many singleton-time modifications have F0-measurable coefficients, and deterministic Borel time functions are predictable. |Z|<=1. Censoring is deterministic and conditionally independent. Exponential event times are independent and continuous, so no tied failures. For s<t, conditional on survival through s, E(N_i(t)-N_i(s)|F_s)=1{T_i>s}(1-exp(-(t-s)))=E(integral_s^tY_i(u)du|F_s), by exponential memorylessness and Tonelli; hence N_i-A_i is a common-filtration martingale, square-integrable since N_i<=1 and A_i<=tau. The Cox intensity at beta0=0 is Y_i(t), including all countable modifications (which do not alter compensator Lebesgue integrals).
counterexample.population: At every t<=tau, Z_i(t) is Bernoulli(1/2) independent of T_i; s0(t,0)=exp(-t), s1(t,0)=s2(t,0)=exp(-t)/2. Thus inf_t s0=exp(-tau)>0, and I=integral_0^tau exp(-t)/4 dt=(1-exp(-tau))/4>0.
counterexample.failure_proof: For each finite n, min_{i<=n}T_i>0 almost surely, so all n subjects are at risk at every t_k for all sufficiently large k. Conditional on their event times, the independent column events E_k={B_1k=...=B_nk=1} have probability 2^-n. The probability none occurs in the next m columns is (1-2^-n)^m, which tends to zero; hence an all-one column occurs after any specified tail index almost surely. At such a t_k, S_n1(t_k,0)=1 while s1(t_k,0)=exp(-t_k)/2<=1/2. Consequently sup_k |S_n1(t_k,0)-s1(t_k,0)|>=1/2 almost surely for every n, and also simultaneously for all n by countable intersection. This measurable countable supremum alone precludes uniform-in-time convergence in probability.
counterexample.bracketing_failure: For f_k(O)=1{T>=t_k}B_k, E|f_k-f_l|>=E|B_k-B_l|-P(T<t_k)-P(T<t_l)=1/2-(1-exp(-t_k))-(1-exp(-t_l)). For all distinct sufficiently large k,l this is at least1/4. A single L1 bracket of width strictly below1/4 cannot contain two such functions, since its width dominates their L1 distance. Thus infinitely many brackets are necessary at that width; finite L1 bracketing is not implied by the intended model.
counterexample.inference_scope: This refutes only the unconditional uniform-time prerequisite. Fixed-time and integrated laws, information and the full terminal estimator expansion remain available; no covariate-class restriction is imposed to evade proof.
counterexample.explicit_bit_realization: For each subject use a Uniform(0,1) variable R_i independent of T_i. Let b_j(R_i)=floor(2^(j+1)R_i)-2 floor(2^j R_i), j>=0, ignoring the null set of dyadic endpoints if desired. Set W_i=b_0 and B_ik=b_k for k>=1. Every prescribed first m binary digits corresponds to one dyadic interval of length2^-m; every prescribed finite subset of digits has probability2^(-number prescribed), by summing the remaining dyadic intervals. Thus all required bits are mutually independent Bernoulli(1/2) measurable functions of one real coordinate. IID subjects may therefore be realized by IID pairs (T_i,R_i) on the usual product sample space, rather than assuming an unconstructed pathological random path.
